why_acceptance_fell: The language filter removed an institutional dump of Polish speeches and replaced it with English archival correspondence — single-page letters with 239-1,606 byte sidecars. The size/HEAD gate correctly routes those to review. Acceptance fell because the candidates got smaller, not because the gate got stricter; IA also returned HTTP 500 on most HEAD requests in this sample.
the_real_problem: subject:"letters" matches personal correspondence — 'Letter to Alice from Uncle Fred, 1918' — not the published letters CHARTER means by 'god source'. Rights, language and format all pass; relevance still fails. collection:americana finds published works ('Antislavery and disunion', 'Miscellanies') but only 2 carry the speeches subject tag, so subject-based querying cannot reach this material at useful scale.
conclusion: The want-list is a better probe and still not a corpus plan. Three filters now pass (rights, language, format) and the fourth — is this the kind of text the Library wants — has no mechanical expression. IA subject tags are folksonomy, exactly as SOURCES.md warned.
